## Design

### 2026-10-11: ## I made a Toadie! A Toad-shaped Starbie!

**8h**

## I made a Toadie! A Toad-shaped Starbie!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/11d5d2343207b7bd662f5df768945ebaecf81e25591a97e30133059d3700080b.png)
Over the course of 3 days and 8 hours of deep-diving into hardware, I built my very first custom PCB for Half-Life: a toad-shaped digital pet I'm calling a "Toadie"!

I started by downloading the care package provided by Half-Life and watched tutorial videos (which I will paste screenshots of below) on installing symbol libraries, footprints, and 3D step files in KiCad. Since I had absolutely no prior experience designing circuits before, stepping into KiCad was a totally new world to me, but working through the guides made it click.

The Schematics & Components

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/d7b2921e550ef31570eb0d76cb43e4e504aa32f0f66a1088b4c61d461749dfbd.png)

I learned how to navigate schematic capture, place components and power symbols, wire up pin connections, and assign precise footprints.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/0566053a9b91440369a650f5ecc632dc8d7f74bdbcf693212d4f0e9e7e60a8dc.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/aa74be56bfc3dfc28d608bbe49e15e409dabde33be2cd40f0f6ed0fb174baf34.png)

Since Starbie is a handheld digital pet, my circuit incorporated:

A XIAO-ESP32-C3 microcontroller

2 Buttons

A DHT11 Environmental Sensor

An OLED display

An MPU6050 motion sensor

Designing the PCB Shape

Once the schematic connections were set, I transitioned to the board editor. I wanted mine to look like Toad, so I used reference images to guide the outline and drew the custom board shape using edge cuts.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/6023bad99910a0a4e8212d066a2ec7be11aa9be3f8e92b9f4aecfcbdf9ccf9cf.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/30173f2033b520f95171dccd0e07dbdbb9f65574daa406ddbd7ea5b36c768948.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/3a2cedc18139cb1ea0bdaa13eb79ea9a4f499ef5d1f7564ce5c3c9605cc341bf.png)
After routing all the copper traces across the layers, I learned how to run a Design Rules Check (DRC) to automatically check for any PCB design mistakes, disconnected traces, or errors, ensuring the layout was completely solid before generating the final views.

I think it took a little over 5 hours to complete the PCB on its own, over  like 3 days.  I watched several youtube videos to learn how to install my files:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/c6093c916451c650fcbe3a6015e0448f7df3f1a943a1fc12f23ac5234bd81095.png)

and how to cut my edge layers.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/4d48fe61dafdf592b332f4c3685df4d3eaeec78838cd0ba32ce5767ee66808e8.png)
Then the last few hours I used them to understand the torturous contraction that is GitHub, specifically how to make a readme, which was harder than it looked! I have SOME experience in markdown, but I was still a little lost on how to add files. I honestly believe getting the repo set was harder than designing the PCB in itself.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/e4c5a0786d440b91b4f75f89bcf9eee5a5a48a8efc241195433af3ba14b85b87.png)

Then finally I was

DONE DONE DONEE

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/031a60feb47b8469404b40a39fe523da29ea2f28550125d17ed5637f747e2e30.png)

### 2026-10-27: I thought I would also include the time it took me to include the feedback I got from my reviewer.

**2.5h**

I thought I would also include the time it took me to include the feedback I got from my reviewer.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/93cc14bab24df65de3168c5ec56ff2af42decb811ad0601a18e015142e2f124b.png)

This was the feedback I received. So I started by figuring out how to embed my BOM both in the README and as a BOM.cvs. The funny thing is at first I used the same code for embedding in the README for the BOM. CVS, but it didn't work, and I just thought my GitHub was acting up like usual; it took me 30 embarrassing minutes to figure out IT WAS TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT WRITING FORMATS. The BOM.cvs uses commas to differentiate. (despite the fact that I am not asking for funding, as shipping to the DRC is SUPER expensive)
